nodeData.note: Learning areas and choosing a pathway.

children.note: Junior school is the three years from Grade 7 to Grade 9. Learners go deeper into subjects, try practical and technical work, and start thinking about careers. At the end, they move on to senior school and choose a pathway.

nodeData.note: Junior school is the three years from Grade 7 to Grade 9. Learners go deeper into subjects, try practical and technical work, and start thinking about careers. At the end, they move on to senior school and choose a pathway.

children.note: The middle step between primary and senior school. It is sometimes called junior secondary school (JSS).
Junior school covers three grades: Grade 7, Grade 8 and Grade 9.

manas.q: Which grades make up junior school?

children.note: Learners join junior school after finishing Grade 6 in upper primary.

manas.q: Which level comes just before junior school?

children.note: The 2019 curriculum framework groups upper primary and junior school together as middle school.

manas.q: Which two levels make up 'middle school' in the 2019 framework?

children.note: The KICD pages we read do not state ages for junior school. Most learners are young teenagers, but ask your school about entry rules.
Subjects are called learning areas. These are the Grade 7–9 areas listed on KICD's current design pages.
Reading longer texts, writing essays and letters, speaking in debates, and using grammar correctly.

manas.q: Name the main language learning areas in junior school.

children.note: Reading, writing, speaking and listening in Kiswahili, including stories, poems and everyday communication.
Numbers, algebra, shapes, measurement and data, used to solve real problems like budgeting or measuring a plot.
Learners study science as one subject that mixes the living world, materials and energy. They do experiments, observe carefully and record results.

manas.q: What is the science learning area in junior school called?

children.note: Instead of separate biology, chemistry and physics, the ideas are taught together. Separate science subjects appear later, in the senior school STEM pathway.

manas.q: Where do biology, chemistry and physics become separate subjects?

children.note: Learners ask questions, test ideas, measure and record. Simple home items like salt, water and a torch can show science at work.
Learners practise handling equipment and materials safely, a habit they need for any science or technical career.
A practical learning area that introduces technical work: using tools and materials safely, making things and understanding the world of work. Check the current design for the exact topics.

manas.q: Which junior school learning area introduces practical, technical work?

children.note: The 2019 framework called it Pre-Technical and Pre-Career Education, linking technical skills with career awareness.

manas.q: What was Pre-Technical Studies called in the 2019 framework?

children.note: It gives an early feel for work like building, electricity or woodwork, which link to the Technical Studies track in senior school.
KICD's Grade 9 Pre-Technical Studies design is marked July 2024 – Revised.
Kenya's people, history, government, maps and environment, plus how citizens take part in community life.
Growing crops, caring for animals and looking after soil and water, often through a school or home garden project.
Art, music, drama and movement: learners create, perform and appreciate creative work.
Learners study one: Christian, Islamic or Hindu Religious Education. It covers faith, moral values and how to live well with others.

manas.q: What do CRE, IRE and HRE stand for?

children.note: Learning to read, write and speak a Kenyan community language, where the school offers it.

children.topic: Foreign languages: Arabic, French, German, Mandarin
children.note: KICD lists designs for these four. Schools offer them only where they have teachers, so ask which ones your school has.

manas.q: Which four foreign languages have Grade 7–9 designs?

children.note: Current KICD pages list fewer areas than the 2019 framework, which had 12 core areas. You may still hear older names like Life Skills or Business Studies; check with your school.

manas.q: Do current KICD pages list more or fewer junior school areas than 2019?

children.note: Junior school learning is active: projects, practical work, discussion and real-life tasks, not just notes.
Learners plan, make and present things, like a model, a garden plot or a short survey.
Working in groups builds communication and teamwork. Each learner should still understand the work themselves.
Field visits, school clubs and talks from people at work make learning real.
Learners use what they learn to help meet a real need in their community, then reflect on it in class.

manas.q: What is community service learning?

children.note: Examples: a clean-up of the market area, a tree-planting day, or teaching younger children about handwashing.
After the activity, learners talk or write about what they did, what they learned and what they would change.
Community Service Learning also appears as a senior school subject in the Social Sciences pathway lists.

manas.q: In which senior pathway does Community Service Learning appear?

children.note: CBC aims to build skills (core competencies) and character (values), not only knowledge.
Communication and Collaboration; Self-efficacy; Critical Thinking and Problem Solving; Creativity and Imagination; Citizenship; Digital Literacy; Learning to Learn.

manas.q: How many core competencies does CBC name?

children.note: Example: in Integrated Science, testing which soil holds water best, then explaining why.
Using a phone or computer safely to find, check and share information, and knowing online risks.
Believing 'I can do this': setting a goal for a hard topic and seeing it through.
The framework names values including responsibility, respect, excellence, care and compassion, understanding and tolerance, honesty and trustworthiness, trust, and being ethical.

manas.q: Name two values the CBC framework promotes.

children.note: KICD has values-based education materials and reports a nationwide rollout. Ask your school how it is used.
Junior school is when learners start matching their strengths and interests to future careers and a senior school pathway.
Notice what your child enjoys, does well and keeps returning to: fixing things, drawing, debating, caring for animals.
KICD's course book lists show three pathways: STEM, Social Sciences, and Arts and Sports Science.

manas.q: Name the three senior school pathways.

children.note: Tracks: Pure Sciences, Applied Sciences and Technical Studies. Suits learners who enjoy maths, science, building and technology.

manas.q: Which three tracks are in the STEM pathway?

children.note: Tracks: Languages and Literature, and Humanities & Business Studies. Suits learners who enjoy reading, writing, people and society.

manas.q: Which two tracks are in the Social Sciences pathway?

children.note: Tracks: Arts (music and dance, theatre and film, fine arts) and Sports Science. Suits learners with creative or sporting talent.

manas.q: Which two tracks are in the Arts and Sports Science pathway?

children.topic: A track = a group of subjects
children.note: Each pathway has tracks, which are combinations of related subjects.

manas.q: What is a 'track' in senior school?

children.note: Strong in Integrated Science and Mathematics? Look at STEM. Love languages and Social Studies? Look at Social Sciences. Shine in Creative Arts? Look at Arts.
Ask a nurse, mechanic, farmer or accountant what they studied and what their day is like.

children.topic: How selection works: ask the school
children.note: Placement and pathway selection rules can change. Ask your school how and when Grade 9 learners choose pathways and schools.
Assessment checks progress during the year and at the end of junior school.
Teachers check learning through observation, questions, projects, portfolios and tests, and give feedback to improve.
Schools may also run school-based assessments during Grade 7–9. Ask your school what is done and how it counts.

children.topic: National assessment at end of Grade 9
children.note: There is a national assessment at the end of Grade 9. Check the current name and timing with your school or KNEC.

manas.q: When is the national assessment in junior school?

children.note: This name is widely used, but we could not confirm it from an official KNEC page. Confirm details with KNEC or your school.
CBC aims to describe what a learner can do rather than only give a mark. Ask the teacher how work is graded and what the levels mean.
Junior school years bring big changes in body, feelings and friendships. Support at home and school helps learners stay well and keep learning.
Puberty can bring mood swings and worry about looks. Calm, honest talks help a lot.
Friends matter more now. Talk through how to say no to risky choices without losing face.
Agree on phone times and private settings. Talk about cyberbullying and never sharing personal photos.
Enough sleep, a simple balanced meal and daily activity help concentration in class.
Class teachers, school counsellors or a trusted adult can help. Seek professional help if low moods last.
Good habits in Grade 7–9 make senior school easier.
Short, daily study at the same time beats long cramming before tests.
Turning lessons into short notes, diagrams or mind maps helps memory.
Cover the notes and try to recall, or use flashcards. This shows what you really know.

manas.q: Which study habit shows what you really know?

children.note: Write questions down and ask the teacher or a classmate the next day.
Break a project into small steps with dates so it is not rushed.
Small, regular support at home matters more than expensive extras.
Ask 'What did you make or find out today?' rather than 'Did you pass?'

children.topic: Support projects with what you have
children.note: Use bottles, cartons, seeds and kitchen items for projects instead of buying new materials.
Boiling water, dissolving sugar and fermenting dough are real science. Ask 'why does that happen?'
Let your child budget for shopping and compare prices per kilo.
Tell your child about your job and skills. It builds career awareness.
Attend meetings, read feedback and raise concerns early.
After Grade 9, learners join senior school (Grade 10–12) in a chosen pathway.
Senior school covers three years for learners about 16–18, per the 2019 framework.

manas.q: Which grades make up senior school?

Review interests, results and school options with your child well before selection time.
Find out which pathways and tracks each senior school offers before choosing.
A new school can feel big. Encourage joining clubs and keeping good study routines from day one.
